title: Section-normalized continuous module presentations
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative topological ring and $V$ a topological additive group with an $A$-module structure. Use the existing condensed continuous-function ring $\underline A$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and the inverse image $p_X^*$ and Cartesian coefficient transport [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A section-normalized continuous module presentation consists of an internal $\underline A$-module $L$, a natural additive isomorphism $L(S)\simeq C(S,V)$ on every profinite set, identifying its sectionwise scalar action with $(r f)(s)=r(s)f(s)$ through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and natural additive charts $(p_X^*L)(U)\simeq C(|U|,V)$ for every scheme $X$ and small pro-etale object $U$. The charts send the actual point-adjunction unit at the profinite test object $X[S]$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] to pullback along $|X[S]|\to S$. A morphism represents an $A$-linear map $f:V\to W$ when its value on every profinite section is postcomposition by $f$. Use the actual canonical inverse-image composition comparisons of [def-sfb-profinite-coefficient-linearization]; the canonical Cartesian lift is [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. This defines a presentation, and does not assert existence for every topological $V$.
